notificationReview.authenticationAndRecipientIsolation: Composition wraps exactly inbox/unread GETs before rate admission and Account. Routes nest in the same allocation. Abort propagates into verification/introspection; a shared signing-key refresh may drain under its own finite timeout but cannot start later introspection for the abandoned request. Recipient queries bind each principal/actor/realm/resource tuple with ordinality; missing decisions deny. Reader identity and active state are checked again at stream/unread final disclosure.
notificationReview.liveAuthority: Stored delivery/item data supplies provenance rather than disclosure authority. Stream, unread, digest subject resolution and dispatcher preparation resolve current subjects and invoke current disclosure; current block/mute/exclusion policy is checked again. Dispatcher rechecks active principal, item, endpoint generation, preferences and lease eligibility around subject resolution. Digest/delivery use the returned disclosed subject fields; inbox has the source concern recorded below.
notificationReview.reuseAndAllocation: One AsyncLocalStorage lifetime and Fuseki allocation includes nested subject reads and closing fences. GraphReadFence reuses equal safe query inputs only within the request and a live native version; SQL/recipient decisions remain live. Sequence/native movement retries within the same budget, with at most six attempts. No cache survives the request. Without native version, inputs are read live.
notificationReview.sqlAndEngineLimits: Store/dispatcher transactions set 2s lock and 5s statement timeouts. Shared pools have finite checkout/session/transaction defaults; cancellation retires an active checkout. The allocation has no independent aggregate SQL-statement/SQL-byte/native-engine-work counter. Existing bounded batches and timeouts are logical limits; WORK_READ_COST explicitly disclaims native query-plan complexity. Real SQL/engine work, post-abandonment drain and mixed-reader capacity were not measured by the blocked public run.
notificationReview.unitEvidenceLimits: The synthetic fifty-subject reuse case performs 54 graph exchanges and 100 live owner decisions. Other existing units cover request isolation, graph movement/no-native fallback, parent budget propagation, Account cancellation, SQL wait/statement retirement, swallowed aborts, deferred work, unread final-recipient replacement and fresh retry. They do not establish fifty real active target notifications, public persona availability, the 100ms public cancellation grace, native engine work or pending returning to zero.

A foreground burst of eight gives background/probe work a turn; one job per tick, catalog enrollment batches of 20, work batches and due-index seeks remain bounded.
